docs/.ipynb_checkpoints/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial-checkpoint.ipynb:211:   "source": "Correct. But `fast` reports no cycles - for that you need a\ncycle-accurate engine. The simplest (and slowest) way is `--model\ncycle`: run the **whole program** on the RTL engine and count every\ncycle. (`--engine` names the core; section 3 lists the choices.) For\nthis tiny GEMM that is a couple of seconds of wall time; for a real\nworkload it is far too slow to iterate on - which is exactly why\nhybrid mode, the rest of this tutorial, exists."
docs/.ipynb_checkpoints/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial-checkpoint.ipynb:258:      "[info] 1.736s elapsed, 7365.783Hz\n"
docs/.ipynb_checkpoints/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial-checkpoint.ipynb:310:   "source": "We will measure on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (VLEN=512).\n\nYou do not have to repeat that choice anywhere else: when a hybrid run\nstarts, andes-sim reads the selected engine's parameters and passes the\nmatching hardware configuration to the fast (QEMU) leg automatically -\nboth legs model the same core. Watch for `vlen=512` in the run banner\nbelow. Engines that cannot pair with the rv64 fast leg (for example\n`vsim:d23`, an rv32 core) are rejected up front.\n\n## 4. Measure the kernel: markers\n\n`--model hybrid` skips ahead at MHz speed, then executes the marked\nregion cycle by cycle on the RTL. The answer is the\n`[marker window_cycles]` line - the exact cycle count of `gemm_rvv` on\nthe real core, a small slice of the whole-program figure above and\nmeasured in a fraction of the time. (The comparison code lives after the ROI and never runs in hybrid mode; the PASS you saw was printed by the fast and cycle runs above.)"
docs/.ipynb_checkpoints/andes_sim_gemm_tutorial-checkpoint.ipynb:532:   "source": "Two views of one kernel: the marker span includes the call instruction\nfrom main into `gemm_rvv`; the PC window starts at the function entry.\nThe cycle counts differ by a handful of pipeline cycles.\n\n## Recap\n\n| Goal                              | Command |\n|-----------------------------------|---------|\n| Verify the kernel (instant)       | `andes-sim run --model fast gemm.elf` |\n| Whole-program cycles (slow)       | `andes-sim run --model cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium gemm.elf` |\n| Engine hardware params            | `andes-sim list engines` |\n| Kernel cycles via markers         | `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium gemm.elf` |\n| Hot-loop report (no markers)      | `./build/hotloops --min-iters 10 gemm.elf` |\n| Kernel cycles via boundary PCs    | `andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger pc --pc-start 0x100078 --pc-end 0x1000c4 --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium gemm.elf` |\n\nFor your own kernel: wrap it with `andes_sim_ROI_begin()` /\n`andes_sim_ROI_end()` from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>` and rebuild - or skip\nthe rebuild: run `./build/hotloops` and copy the `measure:` flags\nstraight into `--trigger pc`.\n\nMore: `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` (5-minute model tour),\n`docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb` (all trigger modes and engines),\n`docs/USER_GUIDE.md` (full reference)."
